node.statement: Let phi:U->E and psi:V->E be source and target coordinate charts centered at x, so phi(x)=psi(x)=0, with E finite-dimensional. Since f(x)=x lies in V and f is continuous, D:=U intersect f^{-1}(V) is an open neighbourhood of x. Hence phi(D) is an open neighbourhood of 0, so choose r>0 with the closed ball cl(B_r(0)) contained in phi(D). For F:=psi composed with f composed with phi^{-1}, F is C^1 on phi(D), fixes 0, and is defined and continuous on cl(B_r(0)). The closed ball is compact in finite dimension, so F(cl(B_r(0))) is compact and contains F(B_r(0)); therefore F(B_r(0)) is relatively compact. Thus F restricted to B_r(0) is a compact map. This stronger shrinkage, in particular f(phi^{-1}(cl(B_r(0)))) contained in V, supplies the compactness hypothesis required by GT-granas-dugundji-thm-8.5-leray-schauder.
